Delta 7 Frame May Be Some of the Wildest out There – Carbon Fiber and Kevlar Woven Into a Skeleton
10 photos
Photo: Delta 7
Bicycle frames come in all shapes, sizes, and abilities. Some are built from steel, others from aluminum, carbon fiber, and titanium. Some are built with round tubes, others with oval tubes, diamond shaped tubes, triangular, square, and more. Heck, even entire bikes can now be CNC machined to life. However, of all the frames I've seen over the years, very few stand out quite like the ones born of Delta 7’s Carbon Strand Grid or “IsoTruss” tech.
I’ll be honest, the only reason why I chose to write this article is because I was recently flashed with a sort of marketing ad for Delta 7’s unique bicycles. Intrigued by the looks, i dove deeper and found out that what makes them so special is the fact that their tubes are completed in a way that breaks the mold in terms of traditional design.
Photo: Delta 7 As we can see in the images in the gallery, a Delta 7 frame is signaled by a wild latticework that aims to give rise to a bicycle that is stronger than traditional ones and lighter too, abilities that, since Delta 7 has been tampering with this tech, have been verified in test and real-world settings. Delta 7 has been working with this tech since 2007.
Now, to understand a bit about what IsoTruss may be, allow me to point out that what we’re looking at here is completed from a blend of carbon fiber and Kevlar strands that are woven together into larger structures that are called Super Strands.
With this aerospace-derived tech, Delta 7 can give rise to frames that weigh as little as 1.9 lbs (0.86 kg) while supporting the same loads as a traditional carbon fiber tube. There’s a little clip below to show this structure in action and how it holds up to pressure .
Photo: Delta 7 But, they aren’t easy to make, with sources mentioning that it can take up to 300 hours to complete a single frame. That’s quite the hours, and as you’d expect, they aren’t cheap; we’ll talk about that shortly.
This isn’t the first time that we see this sort of framework in a product, nor will it be the last. Over the years, countless vehicles and concepts have called upon this skeleton-like gridwork to give rise to lightweight structures, but also ones that allow us to tune particular sections of said product. This is true for the IsoTruss frames too.
While I researched this way of building a frame, I found out that some riders call these the stiffest bikes they’ve ever ridden, and I also discovered that some frames are aimed are road riders while others at the hardtail MTB industry.
Aside from stiffness, Delta 7 also mentions that their frames are also very good at taking damage and doing so in such a way that it doesn’t affect the frame around the area that took the hit. But, I was unable to find out if those sections can be fixed, and if so, how easily.
Photo: Delta 7 Keep in mind that Delta 7 frames, be it the Arantix (2.74 lbs / 1.24 kg), the one aimed at MTB riders, or the Ascend, the road bike, are completed in limited numbers, with some frames running just 16 units deep, some of which have already been purchased, which brings me to my next point.
As I researched these bikes, I discovered that a single frame, no components, can cost as much as $7,000 (€6,300) and complete bikes, nearly double that. Some sources do mention that they can cost as little as $5,000 (€4,450) a piece, but it does matter if there’s a sale going on and if Delta is looking to get rid of them as fast as possible.
All that sounds amazing, but as I explored the Delta 7 magic, I did discover something. I stumbled across an article from bike198, written in 2008, that shows a Delta 7 frame in the poorest condition at the Interbike Dirt Demo.
In the image, we can see that the completed tube has come undone at a joint. While it does look bad, and surely is, it appears as though the resin or glue used to hold the two tubes together gave out. The tubes themselves, on the other hand, look intact. A trip to Delta should take care of that, especially since these babies do have a lifetime warranty on them.
Photo: Delta 7 As mentioned, there are still a few of these frames available to potential buyers, in particular, the road frame; there are six more up for grabs.
The question is: Is this the sort of bike that YOU want? To find out, give Delta 7 a call and see if there’s a way you can take one out for a spin around the block. Be sure to have some collateral to leave behind as you do, because these babies aren’t cheap, as you’ve already picked up on that.
A pretty wild frame design, and one that we have seen on other bicycles and concepts out there, so I don’t think this is the last time we’ll be seeing skeleton-like bicycle frames hitting your visual cortex. Ride safe out there, wear a helmet.

Yamaha Floods the Market with 28 Returning Motorcycles for the 2027 Model Year
58 photos
Photo: Yamaha
Earlier this week, Japanese bike maker Yamaha announced the launch of a new member of the hyper naked family, the MT-125. As a newcomer, it packs a lot of novelties, going from design to the mechanical components and the performance levels.
The bike is held together by a Deltabox frame that holds a 125cc engine, and comes with a new shape of the fuel tank and a redesigned, stretched seat, among many others.
But that's not what concerns us now, as we've already gone through it in an earlier story . What interests us today is the fact that that bike was only a sort of a warm-up party for the flood of models Yamaha announced on Friday.
We got word of no less than 28 motorcycles and scooters making a comeback for the 2027 model year in slightly modified form. That's an important thing to mention as, despite the bike maker calling the release the beginning of a bold new era, we truly aren't seeing anything more than visual upgrades.
Before getting into it, it's worth mentioning that the bikes listed below are part of no less than seven distinct categories, or segments, so make sure to go through them all to see if your future dream ride is on the list.
Photo: Yamaha I'll start with the Adventure category and the two Tenere 700 models, the standard and the Rally. In the case of the former, the only thing that's new is an updated graphic and sleeker styling, while the latter throws in two new colors, Crystal Graphite and Heritage White. The bikes will hit the market in the first quarter of next year.
In the Sport Touring category, there are three Tracer machines to check out: the 9 GT+, 9 GT & Y-AMT, and 9 & Y-AMT. Between them, they will land in the last months of next year (that's right, Q3) with new color choices and updated graphics, depending on the model.
Two bikes will land in 2027 guise in the Sport Heritage lineup. The XSR900 GP adds a new blue hue to the list, just as the XSR900, inspired by French Grand Prix racer Christian Sarron and the YZF-750R of the 1990s.
The GP will be available in mid-2027, while the latter arrives much quicker, in the early months of the year. Both will throw in unspecified modifications to the engine and chassis as well.
Photo: Yamaha As mentioned earlier, the MT-125 is the newcomer in the hyper naked range, but it doesn't step into the new year alone. It is accompanied by no less than four other models: MT-09 SP, MT-09 (and MT-09 Y-AMT), MT-07 (and MT-07 Y-AMT), and MT-03.
There is only one (sort of) fresh supersport bike on the menu from Yamaha for next year, the R1 Race, which lands early next year in a new uniform called Icon Blue. It will join the existing range, which comprises the R9, R7, R3 and R125.
Yamaha offers the widest selection of models for 2027 in the off-road category, where no less than ten models will be fighting for attention from the third and fourth quarter of the year: YZ450F , YZ250F, YZ250, YZ125, WR450F, WR250F, TT-R125, TT-R110, TT-R50, and PW50.
These bikes come with the same visual changes as the others mentioned above, but some of them, namely the YZ450F, YZ250F, YZ250, and YZ125, also get the Monster Energy Yamaha Racing Edition. Yamaha didn't bother detailing what this edition is all about.
Photo: Yamaha Last but not least come the five scooters that will be flooding the market next year: XMAX 300 Tech MAX, XMAX 300 Tech MAX+, XMAX 125 Tech MAX, XMAX 125 Tech MAX+, and NMAX 125 Tech MAX.
They, too, rely mostly on new looks and colors to capture the hearts and minds of riders, but that is probably all that's needed to keep people interested and these models at the top of the food chain.
Yamaha made no mention of whether there will be price changes for all the bikes mentioned above, so if you need to know more about that, the best way to go about it is getting in touch with your local dealer.
The models mentioned above have been confirmed, for now, for the European market, while Americans will have to wait a little longer before learning what they'll be able to enjoy.
Photo: Yamaha We are also keeping an eye on Yamaha and its presence at the upcoming Esposizione Internazionale Ciclo Motociclo e Accessori (EICMA) show in Milan , Italy, in early November. For now, the Japanese are pretty tight-lipped when it comes to the premieres they'll present there, if any.
autoevolution will be on site for what is probably the world's largest motorcycle show to bring you fresh info and photos from the world's largest bike makers, so stay tuned for the most exciting moment of the year for the two-wheeler industry.

He Bought a Chevy Corvette Grand Sport, It Broke Down on His Way Home From the Dealership
14 photos
Photo: TecH MoE | YouTube
A customer has recently had his brand-new Chevrolet Corvette Grand Sport delivered. On his first drive home from the dealership, a mile down the road, the sports car broke down. The GM technicians figured out what went wrong with the car.
Moe had just picked up his all-new Corvette Grand Sport and was driving it straight home, on a two-hour drive, when the glitch that totally confused him happened. What turned out to be a remote-start/key fob loop error completely locked the car down.
When the car completely lost all electrical power a mile down the road from the dealership, at a stoplight, it went completely off and trapped Moe inside. He was in the middle of the road, on a turning lane, with no possibility to move or step out of the car. People passed him by, asking if he needed help, but he couldn't even roll down the window. " It was frustrating, to say the least ," he recalls.
Because the electronic door buttons and window switches were entirely dead, he had to wait about 30 seconds before pulling the mechanical floor lever to escape the cabin. The C8 Chevrolet Corvette features a mechanical emergency door release designed specifically for situations where the car completely loses electrical power, locking you inside or out.
Photo: TecH MoE | YouTube It is a plastic handle that sits flat on the floorboard, right next to the outer edge of both the driver and passenger seats, aligned flush against the door sill plates. You simply pull it straight up to mechanically unlatch the door.
After Moe stepped out of the vehicle to assess the situation, the door closed behind him. Because the electrical system was still completely non-responsive, the exterior electronic touch pads wouldn't work, leaving him locked out on the side of the highway.
Another driver and two policemen helped him out. One of the policemen had a Corvette at home and knew his way around the car and helped him get inside the car with the help of the manual key. The other drove to the dealership to see if he could find help, but by the time he arrived there, it was already closed.
Moe called OnStar to confirm that he bought the and that it had not been stolen. So they reset his Corvette, and he hasn't had any problems since. He has already passed the 500-mile (805-kilometer) mark and all is going according to plan.
Photo: TecH MoE | YouTube Moe contacted a dealership close to his home, but the service technicians were unable to replicate the failure. The vehicle performed normally under their supervision. Dealership technicians and OnStar diagnostic representatives concluded that the vehicle's onboard computers, OnStar modules, and anti-theft systems suffered a localized communication loop error.
They explained that the car’s computer network failed to register the presence of the key relative to the remote start sequence, throwing the anti-theft capabilities into error, so the vehicle died completely, rendering the windows, door locks, and even the hazard lights entirely non-functional, requiring the driver to use the mechanical emergency door release to get out.
When attempting to execute a remote start, the owner left their paperwork and an extra key fob inside the trunk. This combination of factors caused an electrical glitch in the vehicle’s onboard computers. The security and communication systems basically locked out the vehicle, leaving it completely unresponsive.
Even though the security system faulted and locked out the vehicle’s electronic accessories, the car still allowed the engine to crank and start while the extra key fob remained in the trunk. The dealership returned the Corvette with no actual fixes performed, because nothing seemed to need any.
Photo: TecH MoE | YouTube Moe also installed a Uniden R8, one of the most powerful and responsive windshield-mounted radar detectors on the market. He also took his car to a specialized shop in Houston to PPF it and ceramic-coat the wheels, so that they would get the necessary protection and be easier to clean.
His car is finished in Admiral Blue with racing stripes in Arctic White, a color combination offered as a tribute to the original Grand Sport , over a Torch Red and Jet Black interior with GT2 bucket seats. It is the exact spec that he wanted. Four days later, the car was good to go, but the owner delayed pickup by a day due to the weather forecast. Now, he can road trip it without needing to worry about ruining the paint. And he’s got plenty to enjoy.
The new mid-mounted 6.7-liter naturally aspirated LS6 V8 pushes out 535 horsepower (542 metric horsepower) and 520 pound-feet (705 Newton meters) of torque. That is what makes the Grand Sport rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in just 2.75 seconds, run the quarter mile in 10.95 seconds with a trap speed of 124 mph (200 kph), and max out at 201 mph (323 kph).
Moe hasn't disclosed how much he paid for his sports car, but the 2027 Chevrolet Corvette Grand Sport starts at $88,495 in the U.S.

I Finally Bought a McLaren F1 in Gran Turismo 7 and Here's What I Did Next
25 photos
Photo: autoevolution
I just looked at my GT7 dashboard and realized I’ve spent nearly 700 hours in the game since I first got my hands on it a few years ago. It’s no longer as exciting to me as the two new Assetto Corsa titles (EVO and Rally) have more to offer from a driving perspective.
But Gran Turismo 7 still has plenty of advantages, including how easy it is for me to just use the controlled pad instead of installing and removing the Logitech RS50 system every single time.
That won’t be a problem once I’ll have my own room and sim rig, which won’t happen for at least a few months. However, I will likely keep playing GT7 at least until Polyphony Digital makes the switch to GT8.
I still have some unfinished business in here, which includes buying and driving every vehicle available. After today, I’m one step closer to that objective.
That’s because I could finally raise 20 million credits, which is what you’ll need to pay for the McLaren F1 GTR. Before I show you what its first mission was, let me tell you a few things about the latest Weekly Challenges.
Jimny Cup Photo: autoevolution It wasn’t that long ago that we had another event in the Jimny Cup. I had a bad time driving my highly-tuned model with just under 300 hp on tap. I noticed a few other players reported a similar experience, and it might all be a result of all the physics tweaks Polyphony has done recently.
I promised myself I wouldn’t use that setup ever again, which is why I bought a brand-new Jimny for today’s three-lap race in Canada.
I figured 112 bhp would be enough, considering I also bought a weight-reduction package. The Castrol livery felt like a good match for the off-road adventure. Even though I almost fell asleep during the race because of how slow this car is, it was still a better experience compared to last time’s outing.
Scoring 52,500 credits after four minutes and 20 seconds, there was only one question on my mind: will we ever get another snow-covered track in GT7 before support for the game stops? At least I know a surprise like that is coming to Assetto Corsa Rally soon.
Special Event Photo: autoevolution I had just recently V12-swapped my Honda Step WGN for a few laps around Barcelona-Catalunya ahead of the latest Time Trial . With all the chassis upgrades and RS tires on, it was pretty good for its size.
I realized using the same setup for this Special Event might be too much, but I also didn’t want to buy another car and start from scratch. Plus, I curious to see how fast I could go through Suzuka’s iconic 130R corner.
What I failed to realize was that this four-lap battle was about to occur around the East Course layout which is much shorter than the full course. I was in the lead just 45 seconds after the start, and found myself lapping everyone at the beginning of Lap 4.
I’d say this car feels a bit wobbly with all that power (and brakes), but I’d still an engine swap I’d recommend to a friend. You’re looking at a 45,000-credits payout after three and a half minutes of racing, by the way.
European Clubman Cup 600 Photo: autoevolution The European Clubman Cup 600 isn’t just about cars built in Europe: it also takes us over to the fictional Dragon Trail-Seaside Reverse track for four laps. I thought about using my tuned Ferrari F355 for the job, but it was way over the suggested 600 PP limit.
I was keen to get back into a Porsche , and my stock 997 GT3 was just waiting for it to happen. Well, I increased the horsepower output and reduced the overall weight before the race, and then found a stunning recreation of what might be the only 997 GT3 RS 4.0 finished in Aston Martin specific color.
Thank God window shopping doesn’t cost a cent. I needed almost three minutes to take the lead, and finished the race four and a half minutes later.
After scoring 75,000 credits for the deed, I noticed my fastest lap in this car was almost half a second quicker than the world record for the recent Lexus RC F Time Trial at the same track.
Evolution Meeting Photo: autoevolution Ever since living with RWD cars, I’ve began losing interest in Mitsubishi Lancer EVOs and Subaru Impreza WRX STIs. I’d still want one for some snow fun, but I would much rather drive an FR platform anywhere else.
This Evolution Meeting event is scheduled for Monza, where you’ll fight 11 other opponents for a total of four laps. I had an Evo IX for the job, complete with 511 bhp on tap and weighing a mere 2,440 lbs/1,107 kg.
There are two pages of time attack themed liveries to choose from, and I didn’t want to keep using my old Cyber EVO one. Hitting 180 mph/290 kph before Turn 1 was great, having to back off the throttle in the first right-hand corner after the chicane due to severe understeer was not.
Am I the only one who thinks Sugo should have been on the menu this week, too? Anyway, I only needed just under eight minutes for the whole event, and was happy to walk away with 105,000 credits thanks to the Clean Race Bonus.
World Touring Car 900 Photo: autoevolution Interlagos is longer than Sugo, yes, but I still support the idea the latest track in the game could have been the right spot for this World Touring Car 900 event. Imagine running there for 15 or 16 laps total! Since I recently unlocked a 2008 Honda NSX GT500, I wanted to use it for this last race of the Weekly Challenges.
At 796 PP, it’s certainly not the fastest Group 2 car in the game. And it looks simply stunning with the Spoon livery, doesn’t it? I found myself in a strange situation two or three laps into the whole thing: some driver hit the wall right in front of me, we got a yellow flag, and I couldn’t slow my car down in time to avoid a three-second penalty.
I stopped for gas and new tires after eight laps, only to discover I had forgotten to buy the grippiest compound available. Regardless of how hard I tried, I couldn’t close the gap to the leader and ultimately finished 20 seconds after he did.
You will still score 102,000 credits for that kind of result, plus the 500K bonus that comes with getting a podium in all five events. But it’s now bugging me so badly that I just need to go at it again.
McLaren F1 Race Car & Nurburgring Nordschleife Photo: autoevolution I had to sell four of my top-tier cars to afford buying the McLaren F1 GTR. I didn’t care about the Ford Mark IV Race Car or the Corvette Racer Concept, but letting go of the Jaguar XJ13 wasn’t easy. Also, I can always get another Ferrari 499P relatively easy, so that’s not that big of a problem either.
I refrained from selling the Ferrari F40 and the Mercedes CLK-LM, though! I can’t believe it took me so long to buy my first 20 million credits car in GT7. I’m almost certain it used to cost half as much a few years ago, but I’ll have to dig through the archives to get a clear answer.
With 600 bhp on tap and weighing just 2,315 lbs (1,050 kg), this is technically a Group 3 race car. The Harrods livery is still my go-to option for it, and it kind of fits the Green Hell if you think about it. It’s quite a beast out there, although it could benefit from more aero. I couldn’t go flat out through Flugpatz and even crashed while trying to do so.
I only needed four minutes to reach the Karoussel, and 6:44 for the complete lap. That’s eight seconds slower than what I achieved in my tuned 911 GT1. I’m sure switching to a turbocharged setup is an easy fix for that.

Himiway's C3 "Cargo" E-Bike Takes a Different Approach to the Game – Going for Just $1,500
9 photos
Photo: Himiway Electric Bike
These days, the bicycle has become something else, something that has given rise to countless offshoots of functionality with one of the fastest growing and adopted industries being cargo e-biking. But, before we dive deeper into the “cargo” e-bike before us today, forget all about the traditional cargo e-bike styles you may be used to.
For a while, the only cargo-carrying gear the timeless bicycle was capable of taping into were cargo racks, frame bags, and trailers. Then came a shift. We stopped looking at what we can add onto frames and just redesigned them altogether.
As a result, two traditional types started to make their appearance, the long-tail , and long-neck, as I like to call them. The long tails are often signaled by an elongated rear triangle that calls upon a network of tubes to often offer structural support to this section of the bike since it’s often designated for cargo itself.
Photo: Tarran Longtails often include a wide range of accessories which we can add to the frame in order to carry a diverse range of cargo.
This brings us to what I call long-necks, or cargo-mules that elongate the front of the bike, and not the rear, pushing the front wheel out in front feet at a time and creating a platform upon which we can load goods and even carry our children in specialized carriers.
‘Long-necks’ often include less accessories as the larger bay can handle a wider range of gear.
With the electrification of our world, these two styles we’re not disregarded and did fall under the spell of flowing electrons, especially since cargo dos require more power to push or pull around; electric power was a blessing for these bike frames.
Sure, another trend that focuses on cargo-carrying is the SUV e-bikes that some brands are currently focusing on, but that's a story for another day.
Photo: Infinite Mobility But, as time moved forward, we started to see different styles of cargo e-bikes come to life, and today, we dive into one of those ‘different’ ones: Himiway’s C3, an electrified mule that’s a bit more compact than any of the previous frame styles I mentioned. It does, however, display a bit of long-tail magic, with a rear that is slightly elongated.
It’s here that we can call upon a range of accessories to mix and match to our needs but we can also carry a seated person back here , preferably a smaller one like a child that knows how to keep his or her feet out of the spokes.
What I'm curious about is what that central section of the C3 is all about. It appears as tough a person could have a seat here, but from what I can see, it won’t leave much room for pedaling. Maybe it’s a place where you can put your feet while riding under throttle function. This is also where the battery is hidden.
Photo: Himiway Electric Bicycles Speaking of which, keep in mind that the C3 is said to come in with a whopping peak range of up to 80 miles (129 km) on a full charge, which is insane for an e-bike that costs as little as $1,500. Sure, the real world will yield less, especially if there’s cargo on the rear, but even 60 miles is considerable in this price bracket. Zipping around at a full 28 mph (45 kph) is sure to also drain your battery faster, not to mention staying on the throttle.
The presence of a torque sensor also means that the system won’t be wasting any energy and assisting us only as much as the feedback we drive into the pedals, as much as we need.
That top speed is granted by the presence of a rear hub motor that’s rated for a nominal 750 W and can produce a peak of 85 Nm (63 lb-ft) of torque, which are more than necessary considering that we need to be pulling cargo along.
According to Himiway, hills with up to 15 degrees are on the menu here. But to help the motor out a bit, we also have access to gearing, provided by a Shimano Altus derailleur moving a chain up and down a seven-speed cassette. It’s not the wildest setup out there, but it’ll do.
Photo: Himiway Electric Bicycles On the safety side of things, the C3 is equipped with a set of hydraulic brakes, but the design of the C3 is also one that’s aimed at safety. Because of the low-step design, along with the weight of the battery being brought down as low to the ground as possible, the center of gravity is lowered, providing a more stable ground.
The 20-inch wheels with 3-inch cross-section tires also bring the entire load as low as possible, and if I may, the headtube angle also seems quite relaxed on the C3 too. Don't forget about lighting at the front and rear of the C3 too, helping you to see and be seen at night. An LCD display and dual-leg kickstand complete the picture here.
The question is: Is the C3 for you? Well, from where I'm standing, it takes a special kind of rider to make this one their own, and ever since the C3 was launched a couple of years ago, only four riders have decided to leave a review on the manufacturer’s website; they amount to a total of 4.8 stars out of five, so pretty good.
Find one in your area, take it out for a spin, and go from there. Ride safe; wear a helmet.

Not One But a Couple of Reborn Pontiac GTO Muscle Cars Dwell Around a Fictional Race Track in the US
11 photos
Photo: angelguerradesign / Instagram
Even casual automotive fans have probably heard at least once about the iconic Pontiac GTO. But how many people know about its absolute importance for the American muscle car movement?
This model was crucial to the development of the American muscle car sector in particular and for sports cars at large, with the Pontiac GTO being originally a front-engine, rear-wheel drive, two-door, and four-passenger automobile manufactured across just five generations (with a hiatus between 1975 and 2003) from 1963 to 2006. More precisely, the first iteration is establishing the nameplate's quirky 'nose' and also, at large, for popularizing the incipient muscle car market segment during the 1960s.
The Pontiac GTO was different from the Ford Mustang, as the latter was smaller and more compact, but also cheaper, and it created the pony car niche, which always slotted below the muscle cars even though in recent times the boundaries have blurred via stuff like the Ford Mustang Dark Horse SC or the 2027 Dodge Charger Super Bee, among others.
Back to the Pontiac GTO, the definitive iteration that’s enshrined in popular culture is the second generation, which was produced from 1968 to 1972 and had semi-fastback two-door hardtop, coupe, and convertible body styles. This one had all sorts of cool models, including ‘ The Judge .’ As such, it is no wonder that people haven't forgotten about it, right?
That includes the imaginative realm of digital car content creators, as the parallel universes of vehicular CGI are always ready to draw from nostalgia – sometimes more than once. For example, Angel Guerra, a virtual artist better known as angelguerradesign on social media, who has prior experience in automotive design via Bugatti and Rimac, among others, digitally proposed us more than two years ago a modern Pontiac GTO revival.
Even better, the pixel master created both The Judge Pontiac GTO revival as well as a more extreme GTO-R version that could easily muster the courage to fight the Ford Mustang GTD without a second’s thought. Now the CGI expert has decided to circle back to his reborn GTO and show it off with additional colors: red, blue, white, or gray – with or without the racing stripes for some of them.
So, what do you think? Should General Motors bring back the Pontiac GTO for an extreme sports car that’s capable of standing up to the S650 Ford Mustang GTD and its 5.2-liter supercharged V8 churning out no less than 815 horsepower? After all, they have the powertrain know-how to make it happen, as all they have to do is ask Team Corvette to lend them one of the options from the C8 Grand Sport, Grand Sport X, Z06, or the ZR1 and ZR1X. Owner Sells His Stolen and Recovered Audi R8 for $213,000, the Car Loses Just $5,000 in Six Years
24 photos
Photo: Cars and Bids
The past few years have been a rollercoaster ride for this 2020 Audi R8 V10 Performance Quattro, but it just changed hands and probably hopes for a life on the road with less adrenaline. The car was stolen from its owner's driveway and recovered. Despite the spotted Carfax, it still sold for just $5,000 under the sticker from six years ago.
Sometimes, just sometimes, the cars' value doesn’t come crashing down at the speed of light. It is mostly rarity (only 429 units built for the United States), originality, and good maintenance, along with a clean Carfax, that keeps value up. It has been the case for this six-year-old Audi R8 V10 Performance. Well, except for that clean Carfax, though.
One day, as the owner’s father left the keys in to go grab lunch inside, the Audi R8 vanished from the driveway. Some kids reportedly took it for a joyride. Eric, the owner, immediately called the police, and the car was recovered later that day in a nearby town, so it did not spend much time away. Luckily, it was recovered intact.
But the time has come for the car to find a new home, as Eric decided to rotate it out of his fleet. And it did for a price he probably never had even hoped for. He got $213,000 for the car that left the showroom floor six years ago for $218,090, which can’t even be called depreciation.
Photo: Cars and Bids So what did the buyer get for the money? The Audi R8 V10 Performance Quattro Coupe is finished in Suzuka Grey Metallic, which seems white in photos, over a contrasting fully black interior, and rides on 20-inch wheels.
The R8 is equipped with the Sport Seat package. The originally a $5,000 factory option includes 18-way power sport seats in Nappa leather with diamond stitching, Nappa leather across almost every visible interior surface, including the upper and lower dashboard, and the Alcantara headliner.
The high-performance coupe also features a carbon fiber front sway bar, front spoiler, rocker inlay, and exhaust surround trim, along with carbon fiber side blades. The Audi MMI Navigation Plus and the dynamic steering make life on board easier. A Bang & Olufsen sound system provides the soundtrack when the driver has had enough of the V10 orchestra.
Speaking of which, the 5.2-liter V10 with naturally aspirated firepower, which also powers the Lamborghini Huracan , pumps out 602 horsepower (610 metric horsepower) and 413 pound-feet (560 Newton meters) of torque. Those are enough to make it rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 3.2 seconds and max out at 205 mph (330 kph).
Photo: Cars and Bids A seven-speed S tronic dual-clutch automatic transmission, co-developed with Dana Graziano, puts the power down through all four corners with the help of Audi's trialed and tested quattro permanent all-wheel-drive system.
Some chips on the front bumper and some creases on the driver’s seat are signs that show its age. The front splitter and driver-side blade have been replaced due to scratches, and the tires, date-coded 2019 and 2020, need to be replaced. However, the six-year-old Audi coupe has only traveled 12,493 miles (20,106 kilometers) before it changed hands again.
Two keys, the owner's manual, the window sticker, a set of all-weather floor mats, and the factory toolkit are going with the car. All for roughly $5,000 under the sticker. Quite a deal for the seller ...

Someone Created an Open-Source Android Auto Alternative Without Google Play Services
6 photos
Photo: GitHub
Google has seemingly become a lot more committed to improving Android Auto these days - with big things like widgets and work profiles already being worked on - but a new project that landed on GitHub promises something many people didn’t think was possible.
Assuming it works as expected, AARE is an open-source project whose purpose is to deliver an Android Auto-like experience without Google Play Services. As impossible as that may sound, the developer explains on the GitHub page that his implementation allows users to “run apps that Google’s Android Auto keeps out.”
For example, instead of Google Maps and Waze, you can run CoMaps and Organic Maps, while instead of Gemini - yes, the controversial Gemini that has so far delivered such an underwhelming experience on Android Auto - you’re getting another assistant.
The Android Auto experience is powered by an Android phone, and users must connect their mobile devices to infotainment screens with a cable or wirelessly. The Android Auto UI is, therefore, projected on the infotainment screen in a car by the smartphone.
AARE is supposed to offer a similar experience with an “open-source reimplementation of the phone side of Android Auto,” the developer experience. “The phone talks the Android Auto projection protocol to the car’s head unit and draws the car screen itself.”
Compared to Android Auto, AARE also promises to offer weather information powered by Open-Meteo. No account or a Google service is involved, and while users are required to provide an approximate location, those specifically interested in avoiding sharing such data can turn it off.
Android Auto still doesn’t show the forecast on all devices, though it was recently discovered that Google is developing an animated character that’d show the temperature and conditions regardless of aspect ratio and display resolution.
AARE also integrates a passenger mode, which ignores the car’s driving status and allows another user to type a destination without turning off the phone screen while the vehicle is in motion.
This project is still in its early days, and as per the list that shows what’s working and what isn’t, some of the features already implemented haven’t been tested in an actual vehicle. This is why you shouldn’t use this as your daily driver, and considering the project is being documented on GitHub, you should help the developer by reporting any bug you come across while using the app.
It’ll be interesting to see what Google thinks about this project in the first place, as such an idea would mean that users would be able to use their Android phones in their cars without being forced to rely on Google’s services. Degoogling isn’t a new concept, but vehicle cabins have more or less been excluded so far, except a few similar projects, such as Gearslip , whose adoption hasn’t necessarily been overwhelming.

Photo: jlord8 / Instagram
The sporty American carmaker Dodge is currently going through some pretty rough times and only has two model series up for grabs: the 2027 Charger starting at $49,995 and the 2027 Durango kicking off not far away at $43,875.
The family-oriented Dodge Durango crossover SUV remains popular among Mopar enthusiasts, but Stellantis won’t be able to beat around the bush for too long with it since the WD third generation has been around since 2011, no matter how many updates it receives.
Meanwhile, the eighth-generation LB Dodge Charger is much newer, launched for the 2024 model year, but it’s also a hard sell because of the higher prices and the lack of a V8 in the lineup, while the Mustang, for example, is cheaper and has the V8 option on various models. One thing it has going for it, the Charger, is the four-door version.
But it’s hardly a consolation since the internal-combustion Mustang crushed the Dodge Charger during the third quarter of the year in America with 9,960 deliveries to 3,446 sales for the ICE Charger. Anyway, it’s pretty obvious that Dodge needs help, and the rumor mill talks about the brand finally coming back to NASCAR or a Charger SRT Hellcat being prepared for next year.
However, a member of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI has a much simpler solution: Jim, a virtual artist known as " jlord8 " on social media, loves messing around with all things CGI from the automotive realm, and he dreams of a reborn Dodge – the Neon.
The nameplate, which took its name from the chemical element, was sold under the Dodge, Plymouth, and Chrysler brands in various parts of the world, produced on two separate occasions, for the 1995 to 2005 and then for the 2017 to 2020 model years across three generations. The first two had a very distinctive feature which made the Neon easy to recognize: egg-shaped round headlights.
Now, the pixel master wants to bring them back, imagining that Dodge never made the mistake of selling the failed Hornet in North America and instead invested into bringing to market the fourth iteration of the Neon. The CGI expert jumps immediately into action with a sporty version, revealing the Dodge Neon GLHS three-door hot hatchback.
It’s a simple solution – a compact hot hatchback in the same vein as the VW Golf R but with American traits all over the styling. Someone even suggested the perfect powertrain for an eventual R/T version: a four-cylinder turbo with 300 horsepower and all-wheel drive. Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat for Sale, What’s a 2024 MY Worth After 7,000 Miles?
6 photos
Photo: Instagram | imad_mcc
As every gearhead and their pet can tell you, the Hellcat engine is not dead, even if an AI tried to tell me otherwise when I asked it what models featuring the 6.2-liter supercharged V8 are still in production today, because these include the resurrected Ram 1500 SRT TRX and the Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat.
Previous models included the numerous versions of the Dodge Challenger and Charger (the old one), as well as the mighty Jeep Grand Cherokee Trackhawk, but these are dead and buried, whereas Ram’s super truck and Dodge’s super SUV are still a thing. And we are here to talk about the latter. More particularly, the example pictured above, which we just stumbled upon, and as mentioned in the title, it is looking for a new home.
Before delving into the information that the selling dealer released on social media, which is more than modest, let’s talk about the appearance. This Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat sports a glossy black look on the outside from bumper to bumper, with only the red badging on the grille, front fenders, and tailgate providing a bit of contrast. The V-spoke black concave wheels spin around the red brake calipers, and the vehicle features tinted windows that do a very good job at keeping the interior away from prying eyes.
Fortunately, the vendor also released a few images of the cockpit, and unlike the exterior, it is more lively. That’s because it features red leather upholstery on the seats, on the lower parts of the dashboard, and on the center console. There is also black leather upholstery on deck, as well as some white stitching for more contrast, and the seatbelts are red. The SRT emblem decorates various parts of the interior, and the usual gear is on deck.
Photo: Instagram | imad_mcc This Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat has individual rear seats, as we can see from the pictures shared above in the gallery, and does not seem to have any flaws. At least not when it comes to the visual part. Nevertheless, keep in mind that the driver’s seat is only partially visible in these pics, and chances are that it might show some wear on it. After all, the vehicle in question is not exactly brand new, as it has seen some action over the years, although not a lot of it.
According to the vendor, this thing had just under 7,000 miles (~11,250 km) on the clock at the time of cataloging. In fact, the odometer is said to read 6,933 miles (11,158 km), and you are looking at a 2024 model year example of the American super SUV that can give the exotic crossover establishment a run for its money while costing a lot less.
Since we started talking about the performance, we should remind you that the Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat has no fewer than 710 wild horses roaming wild under the hood. The output is in brake horsepower, and it translates to 720 metric horsepower and 529 kilowatts. As for the peak thrust, it stands at 645 pound-feet (874 Nm). That’s how much the mighty Hellcat lump, a 6.2-liter supercharged V8, pumps out with no outside intervention.
Photo: Instagram | imad_mcc But how fast is the Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat? Well, it takes just 3.5 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill, that is almost as fast as the usual performers in the blue-blooded crossover class from Ferrari, Lamborghini, and Aston Martin. These include the Purosangue, the Urus, and the DBX, respectively. The automaker says that the range-topping flavor of the Durango will eventually run out of breath at 180 mph (290 kph), and can deal with the standing quarter mile in a very cool (for such a thing) 11.5 seconds.
Now that we have revealed what we know about the pictured Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat , how much do you think this thing costs? As mentioned above, you are looking at a 2024 model year high-rider, and these used to have an MSRP close to the six-digit territory. Nowadays, they tend to fetch between $65,000 and $85,000 on the used car market in the United States of America. The latter sum is for examples with less than 5,000 miles (8,000 km) under their belts, in pristine condition, whereas high-mileage cars are obviously more affordable.
That still does not answer the question popped in the above paragraph, so how much is this one? Unless you said $84,995, then you are wrong, because this was the asking price at the time of writing. We found this Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat advertised on social media (Instagram) by @imad_mcc, with the dealer saying that shipping nationwide is available, and adding that it offers financing, and accepts trade-ins.
So, if you were shopping for a low-mileage Dodge Durango SRT Hellcat and saw this 2024 model year example, would you blow $85K on it? The 2027 MY SRT Hellcat version of the Durango has an MSRP of $81,495. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Imad (@imad_mcc)
